issue_context.title: like #24694，Interlocked.CompareExchange/Exchange still missing for UIntPtr
comments:
This is the set of .NET 5.0 `Interlocked` methods:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12032350/101771514-5784a080-3aea-11eb-9ec0-6f3411decd12.png)

Maybe we should add `IntPtr` and `UIntPtr` overloads to `Add`, `Increment`, `Decrement`, `And` and `Or`.

Is `Interlocked.Read` still relevant or does `Volatile` cover that? If still relevant, adding `*Ptr` overloads there would make sense, too.
This should be higher priority now that there is the `nuint` keyword.

+1

I was just looking for `Interlocked.Add` with `nint` overload, saddened to see it doesn't exist.

review_comments:
nit: Use `nuint` so this is an identity conversion and doesn't go through the user-defined cast operator.

It will make the IL about 5 bytes smaller and help with inlining. Same if the you do `(long)(nuint)value` instead (so about 10 bytes smaller total)

I thought the plan was the C# compiler will soon start treating nint/IntPtr and nuint/UIntPtr as pure synonyms, at which point there shouldn't be such a difference.  Have I misunderstood?

I'm fine updating this if there's actually benefit, but for now I just stuck with consistency with the existing IntPtr overloads.

That's the plan yes. 

No strong preference on it actually happening if we'd rather wait for the compiler changes, just wanted to call it out as a current inefficiency.
